item.title: Shijimi Clam Miso Soup: The Taste of Lake Shinji — Guide
item.description: Lake Shinji, the brackish lake on the edge of Matsue, is Japan’s leading source of yamato-shijimi, small freshwater clams that are the star of the region’s most beloved dish: shijimi miso soup. The tiny black clams give a deep, savoury broth rich in umami, and the soup is a Matsue staple eaten especially at breakfast — and famous throughout Japan as a folk remedy for a hangover, thanks to the ornithine the clams contain.

item.title: Shimane Food Guide: Izumo Soba, Nodoguro & Lake Shinji Delicacies
item.description: Shimane’s food culture is built on cold water, deep lakes, and centuries of tea ceremony ritual. The prefecture produces some of the most celebrated ingredients in Japan — blackthroat seaperch that Tokyo fish markets pay premium prices for, tiny freshwater clams whose broth is claimed to cure hangovers and revive the weary, and a style of soba that requires a specific pouring technique most visitors get wrong on the first try.
